app.examples.path-placeholder: An absolute path on this machine, such as C:/Users/you/AppData/Local/Temp
app.examples.url-note: This is a URL, not executed through the gateway; opening it in the browser carries the session parameter
app.examples.probe-title: A probe from the example app
app.examples.stale-export: {v1}: core/qxssh-api.js has no such export (the list is out of date)
app.examples.need-host: Pick a target host at the top of the page first
app.examples.group-needs-host: The endpoints in this group need the target host picked at the top
app.examples.show-hidden-risky: Show the other {v1} risky endpoints in this group
app.examples.notes-source: The list lives in sysapi-groups.js, the source of truth for all system APIs grouped by permission node;
app.examples.notes-verify: compare it against the exports of core/qxssh-api.js to see whether anything is missing.
app.examples.notes-default-args: Endpoints run with their default arguments
app.examples.notes-buildargs: The buttons do not pop up an argument dialog: each endpoint's default arguments live in buildArgs(); edit that table to change them.
app.examples.notes-danger: A button styled as dangerous asks once more before running.
app.examples.irreversible-warn: This cannot be undone. Continue? (This example app will not guard it for you)
app.examples.note-hosts: Permission node hosts:read (create/update/delete go through hosts:create/hosts:update/hosts:delete or hosts:manage). An empty host means this machine.
app.examples.note-forget-os: Cannot be undone. If another host still uses it as a jump host, the server refuses and lists the referrers.
app.examples.note-creds: **The only exit for plaintext credentials.** An authorised app can send them anywhere itself. Not demoed by default; you have to type the kind in.
app.examples.note-files: Permission nodes server:read / server:write / server:delete. One set for a normal session and one for elevated (sudo).
app.examples.note-exec: Permission node server:exec / exec:run (remote) / local:exec (this machine, host empty).
app.examples.note-network: A forward listening locally needs tunnel:local / tunnel:list; a remote listener belongs to tunnel:start / tunnel:stop / webproxy:start / webproxy:stop.
app.examples.note-apps: Permission nodes apps:list / apps:validate / apps:install / apps:link / apps:uninstall / apps:toggle.
app.examples.note-perms: Nodes apps:list / perm:read / perm:grant / perm:revoke / perm:clear. perm:granted views self permissions.
app.examples.note-audit: Fine-grained nodes: logs:read / logs:readSensitive / logs:archive / logs:clear / logs:settings:read / logs:settings:write / logs:verbose / audit:note.
app.examples.note-prefs: Global preferences use prefs:read / prefs:write; app private preferences use prefs:self:read / prefs:self:write.
app.examples.note-storage: App dedicated directory storage (non-default, requires authorization): storage:list / storage:read / storage:write / storage:mkdir / storage:rename / storage:delete.
app.examples.note-localfs: **No sandbox** — this hands over the whole machine, SSH private keys included. local:read / local:write / local:delete, risk level 3.
app.examples.click-for-result: (click a button to see the result)
app.examples.floatcard-intro: A raised container with its own outline and light shadow, often used for panels that sit above the main content.
app.examples.field-note: field is only a pairing of a label and a control
app.examples.collapsible-note: collapsed takes the ids of the nodes collapsed initially; after onToggle(id, expanded) fires, this page changes the signal.
app.examples.confirmbar-hint: (A confirmation bar appears here after you click Delete)
app.examples.hostdialog-note: Ten-minute timeout returning {ok:false}; danger:true puts the confirm button in the danger style.
app.examples.icon-search-placeholder: Search icon names (server / eye-off / Docker, say)
app.examples.icon-page-desc: Icons (icon(name)) — click any icon to copy its name
app.examples.icon-resolution-1: Name resolution order: custom icons → the alias table (lowercase name to Lucide PascalCase name)
app.examples.icon-resolution-2: → Lucide native names. When all three miss, it renders a question-mark placeholder and logs once.
app.examples.card-plain-desc: The most basic container: a title plus content
app.examples.card-fill-desc: fill makes the content area take the remaining height
app.examples.card-opts: opts: fill (stretch the content), cls (extra class names).
app.examples.floatcard-hidden-note: You cannot see the content in this cell
app.examples.floatcard-note: floatCard is a component, not a plain function: its visibility comes from props and it holds no state itself.
app.examples.sidebar-flat-desc: Ungrouped blocks — this is the shape the tabs in createAppShell's sidebar take.
app.examples.sidebar-grouped-desc: Several groups with a title, a description and per-row hints — for sidebars with many items.
app.examples.sidebar-group-note: The description text of a sidebar group
app.examples.tabs-note: Tabs is a controlled component: active is held by a signal in this page and onChange only changes that signal.
app.examples.breadcrumb-note: onNavigate gives the index of the clicked segment; the last one is always disabled.
app.examples.chipgroup-note: chipGroup suits "narrow things down", segmented suits "switch between a few views".
app.examples.section-menu: Menu, menu panel and dropdown button (menu / MenuPanel / dropdownButton)
app.examples.menu-note-1: menu is an imperative overlay (you give it coordinates; it mounts to the body through island); MenuPanel is the panel itself,
app.examples.menu-note-2: so you can put it in any container.
app.examples.popper-note-1: openPopper differs from menu only in how it is positioned: menu takes screen coordinates, openPopper takes an anchor element,
app.examples.popper-note-2: measures the position itself and flips at the viewport edge; the panel gets its data and callbacks through props.
app.examples.steps-note: current is the index of the current step, counting from 0; steps before it show as done.
app.examples.section-search: Search box and search select (searchBox / SearchSelect)
app.examples.searchbox-note-1: searchBox skips the events fired while an IME is composing (compositionstart/end),
app.examples.searchbox-note-2: otherwise a half-typed Chinese word triggers the callback and breaks the composition.
app.examples.toolbar-actions-tip: Actions on the right of the toolbar
app.examples.pagination-note: The cell count is fixed: for a given total, the width does not jump whichever page you are on.
app.examples.section-input: Single- and multi-line input (inputField / textareaField / field)
app.examples.inputfield-note: An input keeps its current value in the DOM and a parent repaint will not wipe it; lift it into a signal yourself if the interface has to follow.
app.examples.radiogroup-note: Several RadioGroups on one page must get different name values, or the radios exclude each other.
app.examples.switchtoggle-note: switchToggle is for settings that take effect as soon as you flip them; checkbox is for one ticked item inside a form.
app.examples.section-file-async: File drop and async button (FileDrop / AsyncButton)
app.examples.filedrop-hint: Drop files here, or click to choose (a local demo only; nothing is uploaded)
app.examples.asyncbtn-note: An AsyncButton disables itself and shows busyText while running; exceptions are swallowed into a toast rather than propagated to the caller.
app.examples.table-note: A column can supply render to customise its cell (it returns a vnode); rowKey decides the stable key.
app.examples.listrow-note: active marks the selected state; onDblClick / onContext are optional.
app.examples.jsonviewer-note: The expansion state lives inside the component: opening one level reruns only the JsonViewer itself and nothing else on the page moves.
app.examples.jsonviewer-expand-note: expandAll opens the whole tree on first paint and overrides the maxDepth default; manual clicks still win — overrides live in a Map, so a path you toggled stops following expandAll.
app.examples.jsonviewer-keysplit-note: keySplit takes a regex and splits the key at the first whitespace into a key plus a value suffix; the leaf's placeholder true is no longer rendered. systemd critical-chain uses it to keep trim_init.service as the key and move @19.268s +20.456s into the value slot. The @ value is when the unit became active (measured from kernel start), so it can be multi-part like @1min 44.881s; only the + value is the unit's own start duration, and target units usually omit it.
app.examples.jsonviewer-shader-note: shader receives (text, ctx) and returns tokens, where ctx.slot distinguishes key / value / suffix / root. The second card colours with languageShader('log') by log grammar, the third uses a custom examples-threshold shader that buckets numbers by value; a throwing shader or an empty token array silently falls back to plain text instead of breaking the tree.
app.examples.logpanel-note: lines is a controlled array of strings (not an append handle); once the lines exceed maxHeight it scrolls internally.
app.examples.execresult-note: execResultCard is the single-item version; execResults takes a set and can carry a sum.
app.examples.loadingmask-label: Show the mask (it hides itself after 1.8 seconds)
app.examples.loadingmask-note: The mask covers the whole page (it mounts to document.body through island) and returns { close }.
app.examples.section-kv: Titles and key-value pairs (sectionTitle / keyValue / kvGrid)
app.examples.kv-single-note: Good for one item per line
app.examples.kv-note: keyValue is a single item and kvGrid is a multi-column grid; you can mix them.
app.examples.badge-note: badge marks things inline and statusDot marks a status column; both express severity through kind.
app.examples.statusbar-note: A bit can be a string, { text, tip } or a node; to colour by severity, put a badge in it.
app.examples.alertbar-info: A neutral note; it does not interrupt.
app.examples.alertbar-warning: Something worth watching that does not block you.
app.examples.alertbar-error: It went wrong and needs the user to do something.
app.examples.section-empty: Empty and error states (emptyState / emptyAction / errorState / skeleton)
app.examples.skeleton-note: A skeleton's cls decides its shape: a block by default, skeleton-line for a line, skeleton-avatar for an avatar.
app.examples.section-tip: Text tips and key hints (tipAttrs / kbd)
app.examples.tip-content: This is the content of the data-tip
app.examples.tipattrs-note: tipAttrs(text) returns { dataset: { tip } }, the same source as a component's tip argument;
app.examples.tipattrs-note-2: the tip itself is rendered by the global layer in core/ui.js; components carry no popup of their own.
app.examples.tipattrs-note-3: Key hints name the key by platform: take it from modLabel() in core/dom.js instead of hard-coding Ctrl.
app.examples.iconbutton-opts: opts: tip (hover hint), active (selected), disabled, cls.
app.examples.confirmbar-note: Lighter than a dialog: it suits table-row actions where "you only find out you need to confirm after clicking".
app.examples.dialogpanel-note-1: DialogPanel is the panel dialog() renders,
app.examples.dialogpanel-note-2: and the local stage pins it back into the page so you can see the styles.
app.examples.dialog-note: Rendered by the app itself (dialog), without going through the host.
app.examples.dialog-note-2: actions takes nodes rather than button descriptors; close(result) is idempotent,
app.examples.dialog-note-3: and only the first close triggers onClose.
app.examples.promptdialog-note: Returns a Promise: OK resolves with the input, cancel or close resolves null.
app.examples.confirmaction-note-1: confirmAction is the Promise-based confirmation in core/ui.js (resolves true/false);
app.examples.confirmaction-note-2: ConfirmBar is the inline one and hostDialog is the host-rendered one. Choose by situation.
app.examples.context-note: getHostInfo times out after 5 seconds and returns null; getWorkspaceInfo after 8.
app.examples.boot-wait-init: await onInit, then assemble; the assemble function returns a teardown function
app.examples.boot-no-init: Assemble right away without waiting for init — for apps whose lists do not depend on a session
app.examples.boot-note-1: Both bind the returned teardown to pagehide and guard against a second call — if the app binds
app.examples.boot-note-2: pagehide itself, it runs twice. This window uses bootApp as its entry point.
app.examples.section-windowcontrol: Window controls (windowControl / getWindowRect, which return results)
app.examples.wincontrol-note: getWindowRect times out after 5 seconds and returns null; setWindowRect is one-way and clamps what you write to the viewport and the minimum size.
app.examples.section-appearance: Appearance (one-way messages; they apply locally at once and broadcast to every window)
app.examples.appearance-glass-note: The blur opacity goes through set-glass and lives in qx-glass-a (range 0.4–1.8, default 1).
app.examples.notify-note: notify times out after 8 seconds and returns false; writeClipboard after 5. System notifications need the browser to have granted permission.
app.examples.section-hostdialog: Host dialog (hostDialog, rendered by the host)
app.examples.section-hostservices: Host services (pickPath / listApps / listWindows / openApp / openSettings)
app.examples.pickpath-note: pickPath lets the user choose a path in the file manager, resolves null on cancel, and has no dedicated bridge message.
app.examples.perm-note: Five-minute timeout returning false; concurrent requests merge into a single dialog. System apps and the host pass automatically and need no request.
app.examples.themechange-done: Subscribed to theme changes (it fires with the current theme straight away)
app.examples.themechange-note: Put the returned unsubscribe into onUnmount, or the subscription outlives the window.
app.examples.section-appapi: Inter-app APIs (provideApi / revokeApi / callAppApi / callAppApis / listAppApis)
app.examples.appapi-provided: examples.echo registered; other apps can call it
app.examples.appapi-note: When the target app is not open the host opens a window for it via autoOpen; the result only carries structured-cloneable data.
app.examples.appevent-slow-provided: examples.slow registered: reports progress every 500ms, 5 steps; aborts when the caller cancels. Open a second window of this app and call it with callAppApi.
app.examples.appevent-subscribed: Subscribed to examples:* events and this window's state (minimize / maximize / restore and watch the result box).
app.examples.appevent-note: Events are broadcast without acknowledgement and the publisher receives its own; after cancelling, the call rejects with code = cancelled and the provider's ctx.signal fires.
app.examples.fmt-note: The time helpers take either a millisecond timestamp or a Date; rate/dur round internally to whole units.
app.examples.esc-note: Always run esc before assembling HTML — icon() returns an HTML string, so it may only go into h()'s html property.
app.examples.storage-note: Your own data goes through the storage/* endpoints under appdata/<app id>/ and is removed with the app; shell-level preferences go to prefs.js. Do not mix them.
app.examples.signal-note-1: signal is the smallest reactive primitive: changing the value reruns only the component that read it;
app.examples.signal-note-2: a computed lists its dependencies explicitly (these primitives do no automatic collection).
app.examples.section-getinfo: Host info (getInfo(), a public read-only endpoint in core/qxssh-api.js)
app.examples.getinfo-note: This is /api/v1/host/version, the only business endpoint without auth; it suits a version badge.
app.examples.task-note: task handles the toast and the button busy state; a failure toasts the error too, so the caller needs no try/catch of its own.
app.examples.selfcheck-desc: Compared both ways against the actual exports of components.js: what the classification misses (not demoed) and what it lists that does not exist (stale list) must both be empty.
app.examples.selfcheck-ok: Every component is classified and demoed.
app.examples.dialogpanel-note-3: DialogPanel does not mount itself: dialog() mounts it to the body through island, and close() tears the tree down before detaching the host.
app.examples.selfcheck-desc-api: The endpoint list is compared both ways against the exports of core/qxssh-api.js: what it misses is a new endpoint (not demoed), what it lists that is absent is a stale entry. Language negotiation and the appStoreRead variants do not count — they are not separate endpoints.
app.examples.selfcheck-api-missing: In qxssh-api.js but not in the list: {v1}
app.examples.selfcheck-api-unknown: In the list but not in qxssh-api.js: {v1}
app.examples.selfcheck-api-ok: Every endpoint is in the list.
app.examples.kit-note: The toolkit is built on the generic exec/* and net/* endpoints; the backend has no domain endpoints at all. sudo:'auto' only asks for a password on a permission failure. The second row shows manifest.apis declarations launching closed apps; terminal.open asks the user for term:open first.
app.examples.platform-intro: Exports of core/* and the bridge that are neither endpoints nor components, module by module: buttons run once and echo the result, live widgets sit inside the card; names marked as shown elsewhere are not repeated, names marked internal belong to the host runtime. The self-check at the bottom compares both directions against each module's real exports.
app.examples.platform-need-host: This demo needs a workspace host
app.examples.platform-internal: Host / runtime internals, not called by apps: {v1}
app.examples.platform-qx-missing: On qxssh-sdk.js but in no module registry: {v1}
app.examples.platform-ok: Every export is registered (demoed, marked as shown elsewhere, or marked internal).
app.examples.platform-selfcheck-desc: Each module is imported whole as the reference and compared both ways with the registry; qxssh-sdk.js is only a re-export surface, every name on it must be found in some module.
app.examples.pf-note-bridge: The bridge between app and host. Most capabilities are demoed on the Host page; this card adds context, window rect, API-change subscription and pre-first-paint theme / glass sync.
app.examples.pf-note-kit: Heavy-app toolkit: run and parse commands, chunked streams, raw TCP, HTTP via the target. An empty host means the local machine.
app.examples.pf-note-i18n: i18n runtime. setLang switches this app's own language (it has a scope); the internal ones are driven by setupI18n and the host.
app.examples.pf-note-i18nui: Ready-made language switchers and the re-render-on-language wrapper. Do not hand-roll switchers.
app.examples.pf-note-signal: Reactive primitives: effect collects dependencies, batch coalesces writes, untrack reads without subscribing.
app.examples.pf-note-vdom: Virtual DOM entry points and helpers. Portal teleports a subtree, vnodeHTML serializes a vnode for debugging and assertions.
app.examples.pf-note-dom: DOM and formatting helpers. isMod picks the modifier per platform (metaKey on macOS, ctrlKey elsewhere).
app.examples.pf-note-prefs: Shell-level preferences: SQLite is the source of truth, localStorage only a write-through cache. Note: apps run in the sandbox (an opaque origin), where localStorage throws and silently degrades to an in-memory cache; an app's own settings belong in its private storage. Keys carry the qx- prefix; the demo key is deleted afterwards.
app.examples.pf-note-store: Host store: the host list the shell loaded and the current workspace. setWorkspace / clearWorkspace are called by the desktop page.
app.examples.pf-note-sys: The system-API call core: session, automatic permission prompts on 403, sudo elevation. Every core/qxssh-api.js function is a thin wrapper over these.
app.examples.pf-note-tunnels: Port-forwarding wrappers (validation, type labels, start/stop). The startTunnel demo starts a SOCKS5 on a free port and stops it immediately.
app.examples.pf-note-dataview: Data view: load → render → empty / error / loading → polling, with single in-flight and race protection built in.
app.examples.pf-note-splitter: Draggable splitter: adjusts the panel's flexBasis, persists the width, double-click resets.
app.examples.pf-note-stream: Consumer side of chunked streams: line buffer, log rendering (auto-scroll only when at the bottom), streaming by URL.
app.examples.pf-note-bus: In-page synchronous event bus. Cross-app events go through the bridge's publishEvent / onEvent, not this.
app.examples.pf-note-readstream: Hands a Response body to a callback chunk by chunk, in arrival order.
app.examples.pf-note-terms: Key first, Chinese fallback: backend-issued labels (permission nodes, categories) carry both; the term is used when present.
app.examples.pf-note-clip: Clipboard write (with the insecure-context fallback). The bridge's writeClipboard is the host-performed variant.
app.examples.pf-note-storage: Thin JSON wrappers over localStorage. Inside the app sandbox (an opaque origin) localStorage is unavailable and these degrade silently (reads fall back to defaults, writes are ignored). App data belongs in private storage (storage/*); this is for transient UI state only.
app.examples.pf-note-ui: In-page feedback: toast, confirm, copy, tasks with feedback. Used throughout the component pages.
app.examples.pf-note-shell: The app page skeleton. This app itself is built with it (see the boot section of app.js).
app.examples.pf-note-icons: Icon exports: icon renders SVG by name, appIcon adds the fallback for app-supplied icons.
app.examples.pf-note-apptext: Localized app-manifest text: name / description / category may be per-language objects; read them through here, never directly.
app.examples.pf-note-probe: Target-host metrics and hardware info: a marker-delimited script runs remotely via exec/run and is parsed in the frontend (the former host/metrics and server/hostinfo endpoints are gone). parse* are pure functions; sample text is fed here.
app.examples.pf-note-wall: Wallpaper list and user wallpaper add/remove: the built-in list is a static index.json, user wallpapers go through localfs/* (the former wallpaper/* endpoints are gone). The upload / delete demo uses a 4-byte examples-demo.png; deleting restores the state.
app.examples.pf-note-code: Zero-dependency syntax highlighting: CodeEditor is the multi-line editor (line numbers, Tab indent, auto-indent on Enter, Ctrl+Enter to submit, read-only), codeField is the single-line input for forms, highlightCode the read-only block. Built-in sh / yaml / json / nginx / sql / ini / dockerfile / js / go / log; registerLanguage adds your own.
app.examples.note-secret: Put passwords and tokens here instead of private storage: values are encrypted at rest, isolated per app, and verbose audit never captures the write body. secrets:use is a default capability.
app.examples.app-reload: Reload all windows of this app
app.examples.args-abs-dir: Absolute directory path on the server
app.examples.pf-note-vlist: Virtual list: fixed row height, only rows inside the viewport are rendered, so 100k rows cost a few dozen nodes. The parent must give a definite height; use listRef with scrollToRow to jump to a row.
app.examples.pf-note-charts: uPlot line chart wrapper: the library loads on demand (nothing downloaded until the first chart), colours follow theme variables and the chart rebuilds on dark-mode switch. timeSeries is a fixed-size rolling window: push a frame and hand data() to LineChart.
app.examples.sdk-intro: Unified SDK (qx namespace) aggregates host bridge, operations toolkit (qx.kit), i18n, common dialogs, and advanced components.
app.examples.sdk-playground-desc: Select preset code or write your own calls, click 'Run Code' to see real-time output.
app.examples.sdk-selfcheck-ok: All SDK methods are covered (100% coverage)
app.examples.sdk-selfcheck-note: Self-check: all {v1} top-level exports of the qx namespace have a registered demo entry on this page; {v2} entries in total, covering qx.xxx() methods, constant objects and namespace aliases.
app.examples.codeeditor-note: Supports JavaScript / JSON / Shell syntax highlighting, line numbers, language switching, and read-only mode.
app.examples.codefield-tip: Compact inline code input field with syntax highlighting
app.examples.virtuallist-note: Supports smooth scrolling for 10,000+ items, rendering only visible viewport rows.
app.examples.linechart-note: High performance Canvas/SVG chart rendering with real-time multi-series data point streaming.
app.examples.dataview-note: DataView encapsulates async loading, skeletons, empty states and retry; createSplitter supports draggable pane resizing.
app.examples.i18n-ui-note: Out-of-the-box language switcher select, toggle buttons, and popup menu components.
app.examples.sideaction-note: Used for fixed actions at the bottom of sidebars (e.g. create, collapse, config).
app.examples.note-i18n: System language listing and negotiation APIs.
app.examples.permgroup-hosts-desc: Manage host inventory, probing, credentials, and connectivity
app.examples.permgroup-files-desc: Browse, read, upload, download, move, and delete remote files
app.examples.permgroup-exec-desc: One-shot execution, live streaming, long sessions, and interactive terminal tunnels
app.examples.permgroup-job-desc: Start, query, follow, and terminate persistent background jobs
app.examples.permgroup-schedule-desc: Manage cron-like task schedules and trigger executions
app.examples.permgroup-network-desc: HTTP proxying, intranet web reverse proxy, and raw TCP bridges
app.examples.permgroup-storage-desc: Read and write app-isolated persistent files on the server
app.examples.permgroup-secret-desc: App-isolated encrypted credentials and secret key-value pairs
app.examples.permgroup-prefs-desc: Read and write system-wide and app-private user preferences
app.examples.permgroup-apps-desc: List, validate, install, symlink, and toggle applications
app.examples.permgroup-sudo-desc: Request and clear administrative sudo sessions on managed hosts
app.examples.permgroup-perm-desc: Inspect, grant, revoke, and clear permission scopes
app.examples.permgroup-audit-desc: Inspect audit trails, configure retention, and toggle verbose mode
app.examples.permgroup-local-desc: Query host machine info and read/write local filesystem paths
app.examples.permgroup-public-desc: Public utilities and runtime introspection without special permissions
app.examples.api-search-placeholder: Search API endpoint, permission, or description (e.g. listHosts / sftp / exec)...
app.examples.sdk-search-placeholder: Search SDK method, permission, or description (e.g. qx.host / runLines / alert)...
app.examples.component-search-placeholde: Search component name or category (e.g. Button / Table / Tabs / Dialog)...
app.examples.search-empty-desc: Please try searching with different keywords
app.examples.local-dir-placeholder: An absolute path on this machine, such as C:/Users/you/AppData/Local/Temp
app.examples.danger-confirm: Are you sure you want to perform dangerous action "{v1}"?
